summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis s/p gastric pacer, and hypertension was admitted for nausea and vomiting, unable to tolerate oral intake. The flare was attributed to discontinuation of metoclopramide due to lack of generic prescription coverage. She was treated with IV fluids, antiemetics, and restarted on metoclopramide, leading to symptom improvement. Her insulin regimen was adjusted due to reduced oral intake, and she was restarted on clonidine for blood pressure control after clarifying safety with lisinopril. She advanced to tolerating toast and ginger ale, with stable vital signs and improved hydration. She was discharged home with updated medication instructions, a gastroparesis diet handout, and follow-up plans.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
